title: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
statement: `flights[i] = [from, to, price]` is a directed flight. Return the cheapest price from `src` to `dst` using at most `k` stops. A stop is an intermediate city, so you may use at most k + 1 flights. Return -1 if no such route exists.
hints: Plain Dijkstra by price can take a cheap path with too many stops and then miss a legal path.
Bellman-Ford relaxed for exactly one more edge per round respects the stop limit.
Copy the distance array before a round so a path cannot use more than one new edge in that round.

approaches.name: DFS with pruning
approaches.explanation: Try every walk of length at most k + 1.

editorial: Let dist[v] be the cheapest price to reach v with the flights used so far. Perform k + 1 rounds. In each round, relax every flight against a snapshot of the previous round, so one round adds one flight. If dst is still infinite, return -1.

examples.explanation: One stop allows 0-1-3 for 700. The cheaper 0-1-2-3 uses two stops.
Both the direct flight and the one-stop flight are legal. 200 is cheaper.
